summary: Add customer_note column, backfill, deploy new app, retire old app, drop note column, with a plpgsql trigger to synchronize note and customer_note during concurrent traffic.
write_consistency: Old app writes to note, new app writes to customer_note; a PostgreSQL trigger bidirectionally syncs the columns so that reads from either version see the most recent write, satisfying the runner’s consistency checks.
revision_notes: Root cause: The previous plan’s dual-column schema (note + customer_note) caused the runner’s cross-version read/write checks to fail because writes from one version target a column the other version does not read; backfill only equalized initial values, not ongoing concurrent traffic. Revised plan adds a plpgsql trigger during the expand stage to keep note and customer_note in sync bidirectionally, enabling the runner’s consistency model to pass.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and bidirectional sync trigger
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS \$\$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, '') THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(NEW.note, '') THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; \$\$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_on_write AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Copy all existing note values into customer_note
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Deploy the new‑staged app version (code already updated to use customer_note)
Retire the old app version that only knows the note column
Drop the note column after old app retirement
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
